OmaStats 1.7 shows which drive is slowing your machine down and why. The Disks page groups internal, external and network drives, shows each drive's latency, queue and the processes using it, and finds setups that make an SSD slow, with a button to fix each one. The Memory page gains a pressure ring.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.7.0/omastats-v1.7.0.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

![The Disks page with internal, external and network drives, two problems with Fix buttons, and a drive stalling the system, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.7.0/omastats-1.7.0-disks-dark.png)

## New

- **Find out which drive is freezing your desktop.** Click a volume to see its drive: read and write rates and history, how long each request takes, how many are queued, how much of the time it is busy, and the processes with files open on it. The page also shows I/O pressure, the share of time tasks wait for storage, and marks a drive red when it is busy nearly all the time while every task waits on it. That is the stall that makes a desktop freeze during a big build. Click the volume again to see all disks. By @crmne.
- **Problems that make a drive slow, with a Fix button for each.** OmaStats finds an SSD under an encrypted volume that was unlocked without allowing discards, so TRIM never reaches it even though `fstrim` reports success; an SSD that is never trimmed at all; and a FAT drive mounted with `flush`, which makes every file written wait for the drive. The button opens a terminal that shows each command and asks before running it with `sudo`. By @crmne.
- **Drives grouped as internal, external and network.** USB and Thunderbolt drives are listed apart from the ones inside the machine, and NFS, SSHFS and rclone mounts now appear with SMB shares under Network. A share that stops answering is skipped instead of holding up the panel. The folder button beside each volume opens it in Files. By @crmne.
- **Memory pressure ring.** The Memory page shows how much of the last ten seconds tasks spent waiting for memory, next to the Memory and Swap rings. Used memory alone cannot tell you whether the machine is short of it; waiting can. By @crmne.

![The Memory page with Swap, Memory and the new Pressure ring, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.7.0/omastats-1.7.0-memory-pressure-dark.png)

## Fixed

- **GPU and disk readouts no longer vanish when settings are shared between computers.** Settings synced from another machine named that machine's GPU and drives, so the bar showed no GPU and no disk readout. When none of the saved devices exist, the bar and Settings now use this machine's own, and the saved choice stays for the computer it came from. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- The processes on a drive are your own, found through the files they have open when OmaStats looks, so a process that opens and closes files between samples can be missed. A process with files on two drives shows its total I/O on both.
- Network shares have no transfer counters, so selecting one shows only its processes.
- Allow TRIM rewrites the encrypted volume's settings only for LUKS2. Other encrypted volumes get the advice without a button.
- The FAT fix covers drives mounted through UDisks (under `/run/media`). Other FAT mounts get the advice without a button.
- The process search and color fields take typed text only: there is no paste or text selection.
- GPU process lists from open drivers show only your own processes. An integrated AMD card's own load figure jumps between 0% and 100%, so it can disagree with its process list.
- CPU power on Intel, and on AMD without integrated graphics, needs a udev rule that makes `/sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` readable.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.

## Thanks

Thanks to everyone running OmaStats and reporting what they see. The disk checks come from tracking down real freezes and slow copies on our own machines.

Both bundled binaries are rebuilt twice in CI, compared byte-for-byte with the committed executables, and covered by checksums and GitHub build attestations.
